**Agent**: code-critic
**Notes**: video code is full of 'works on my machine' traps. The critic's job here is to surface the things you'll only see on a real device with throttled network and a low battery.

title: 6.2 Vertical full-screen feed + prefetch + HLS
description:
The player. `PageView` (vertical) with a small pool of `video_player` / `better_player` controllers, aggressive prefetch of the next 2-3 clips, HLS adaptive bitrate so playback never stalls on a bandwidth dip.

**Files**
- `app/lib/features/feed/feed_page.dart` — the `PageView` + controller pool.
- `app/lib/features/feed/feed_item.dart` — single-item widget with overlay (caption, like, follow).
- `app/lib/features/feed/prefetch.dart` — next-N prefetch logic.
- `app/lib/core/video/` — controller lifecycle helpers.

**Validation (the hard ones)**
- Smooth scroll: 60fps on a mid-range Android (Pixel 5 / Galaxy A52 era) when swiping through 20+ clips. Profile with `flutter run --profile` and DevTools.
- No stalls on throttled 3G: Fast 3G profile in DevTools, swipe 10 times → every clip plays without a buffering spinner longer than ~250ms.
- Fast first frame: from swipe to visible first frame < 300ms when the next clip is already prefetched.
- Memory: scrolling 50 clips doesn't blow past ~250 MB on the same device.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is THE task. If you only have time to do one thing well, do this. Single-controller-per-clip is the most common Flutter video mistake — it leaks memory and stutters on scroll. A pool of 3-4 controllers is the right shape.

title: 6.1 Mux integration: signed direct-upload + webhook
description:
Server-side: a Supabase Edge Function that creates a signed Mux direct-upload URL, plus a webhook handler that updates `videos` with the `playback_id` and `status` on `asset.ready`.

**Files**
- `backend/supabase/functions/mux-upload/index.ts` — Edge Function: create Mux direct upload, persist a `videos` row in `uploading` state, return the signed URL to the client.
- `backend/supabase/functions/mux-webhook/index.ts` — Edge Function: verify Mux signature, update `videos.status` and `videos.playback_id` on `video.upload.asset_created` / `video.asset.ready`.
- `app/lib/features/upload/` — Flutter upload widget that PUTs the file to the signed URL with progress + retry.

**Validation**
- End-to-end: pick a clip on device → progress UI shows upload → within ~30s the `videos` row flips to `ready` and a `playback_id` is present.
- Webhook signature verification: a forged webhook returns 401.
- Failed upload (e.g. Mux rejects the file) flips the row to `errored` and is visible in a 'your uploads' debug screen.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: use Mux's signed direct upload (not the public upload) — the whole point is that the Supabase service-role key never leaves the server. Webhook signing-key verification is non-negotiable.

title: E7 — Phase 6: Video feed end-to-end (MAKE-OR-BREAK) (Part B · app) [~2-4 weeks]
description:
**Phase 6 (Part B · app) — ~2-4 weeks · priority HIGH · MAKE-OR-BREAK**

The defining feature of the app. TikTok-style vertical full-screen feed, video uploads via Mux signed direct-upload, HLS playback with a controller pool and aggressive prefetch. If this phase doesn't ship, the app doesn't ship.

**Why this is high priority and big-effort**: video is the hard part. Networking, codecs, scroll perf, prefetch, signed URLs, webhooks, error states, and analytics all collide here. A 'simple feed' prototype is achievable in a week; a *smooth* feed that doesn't stall on throttled 3G is a multi-week effort.

**Ordering note**: depends on E6. Children 6.1 and 6.2 are the critical path; 6.3 (ranking) and 6.4 (review) are parallel-friendly.

title: M.1 Run the finished agent against the architecture spec
description:
The bridge moment. Run the agent end-to-end against `docs/architecture.md` and the constraints (solo dev, no hard deadline, Flutter, Supabase, Mux).

**Inputs**
- `docs/architecture.md` (the locked spec).
- Constraints passed as flags/env: `--max-depth=4`, `--node-budget=200`, `--target-stack=flutter,supabase,mux`.

**Outputs**
- `docs/backlog/index.md` + per-epic Markdown files + `docs/backlog/backlog.json`.
- A `docs/backlog/critic_report.md` with the bounded critic's findings.

**Validation**
- Every leaf in the produced tree has `estimate_days <= 1.0` and a clear done-condition in `description`.
- The tree covers all the E0..E10 epics in this roadmap (i.e. the agent agrees with the structure you had in mind, possibly with renames).
- The critic report has no open P0/P1 findings; if it does, they are either resolved or escalated.
- Re-running the agent produces zero diff in `docs/backlog/`.

**Agent**: code-puppy (running the agent CLI).
**Notes**: this is a milestone, not a routine task. If the leaves aren't atomic or the critic finds structural problems, **fix the agent first** (loop back into E2-E4), do NOT 'just continue and clean up the backlog manually'.

title: E5 — Bridge Milestone: agent generates the app backlog (Part A -> B) [~1-2 days]
description:
**Bridge Milestone (A -> B) — ~1-2 days · priority HIGH**

The whole point of building the agent first: feed it the locked architecture spec and let it produce the day-sized backlog for the app, written to `docs/backlog/` with human approval.

**Why this is a separate epic**: it is the only moment in the project where Part A and Part B connect. If it works, the rest of the project is a backlog. If it doesn't, the agent isn't actually useful and you need to fix it before building the app on top of a shaky foundation.

**Ordering note**: depends on E4. Single-task epic.

**Accounts to provision**

- Supabase project — needed by E5/E6 onwards.
- Mux account (default video provider; Cloudflare Stream is the budget swap) — needed by E7.
- **Apple Developer Program ($99/yr)** — needed before any iOS build/distribution (E6+).
- Google Play developer account (one-time $25) — same for Android.
- Sentry, PostHog — observability + product analytics from day one.

**Validation**
- All keys present in `.env`, none in git (`git status` clean for `.env`).
- `supabase login && supabase link --project-ref <ref>` succeeds locally.
- A throwaway Mux signed-upload call returns a usable URL.

**Agent**: owner (you, manually).
**Notes**: do this BEFORE E1 so the agent's smoke tests can hit real services if you choose to wire that. Store keys in `.env` — never commit.

Manage developer/agency records.

**Why:** Developers own projects; needed before project management.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Create/edit/list/delete with validation

**Spec:** §3.2

title: 6.3 Upload validation (size/type limits) + abuse guard
description:
Enforce strict size/type validation and basic abuse protection on uploads.

**Why:** Prevents abuse and malformed media.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Type + size limits enforced server-side

**Spec:** §12

title: 7.6 Security headers (csp:true, HSTS, etc.) via adapter/_headers
description:
Enable Astro 6 stable CSP plus standard security headers.

**Why:** Hardens the static surface.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] csp:true enabled
- [ ] HSTS/X-Content-Type-Options/Referrer-Policy set

**Spec:** §3.1, §12

title: 2.5 Admin LiveView shell + layout + role-gated nav
description:
Build the admin application shell, layout, and navigation gated by role.

**Why:** Container for all catalog management UIs (E4).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Authenticated admin layout with role-aware nav

**Spec:** §3.2

title: 5.5 Search endpoint /api/v1/search + /api/v1/listings?bbox=
description:
Provide full-catalog search/filter and map bbox queries for client-side islands.

**Why:** These dynamic responses need not be indexed (SEO pages are prerendered).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Search with facet filters
- [ ] bbox query returns map markers

**Spec:** §3.1, §4, §8

title: 4.5 Map pin picker in admin for manual lat/lng correction
description:
Embed a map in the admin form to verify/correct geocoded coordinates.

**Why:** Geocoding (E11) auto-fills; humans correct edge cases.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Draggable pin writes lat/lng back to the record

**Spec:** §8

title: 3.6 Seeds + factories across property types
description:
Provide dev/test seed data and factories spanning apartment/land/commercial/rental.

**Why:** Enables building UI, API, and frontend against realistic multi-type data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Seed script + ExMachina-style factories for each property type

**Spec:** §6

title: 5.6 Rate limiting + Cloudflare proxy for api subdomain
description:
Put the public API behind Cloudflare and rate-limit client endpoints.

**Why:** DDoS/WAF protection + edge caching of read endpoints.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] api.subdomain proxied via Cloudflare
- [ ] Rate limits on search/lead endpoints

**Spec:** §11, §12

title: [Immo] E6 — Media Pipeline & Object Storage [~3-5 days]
description:
Upload media to R2, generate derivatives, enforce limits, and back up to Hetzner Object Storage.

**Why:** Media served from R2 next to the static site (no egress fees); backups stay in EU.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Uploads land in R2 via S3 client
- [ ] Derivatives generated async
- [ ] Backups configured

**Spec:** §3.4

title: 3.4 media schema (r2_key, kind, position) + associations
description:
Model media attached to projects and listings.

**Why:** Photos, floor plans, brochures live in R2 and are referenced by key.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] media schema + polymorphic-ish associations + ordering

**Spec:** §6, §3.4

title: E10 — Phase 9: Polish & cross-cutting (Part B · app) [~2-4 weeks, ongoing]
description:
**Phase 9 (Part B · app) — ~2-4 weeks, ongoing · priority normal**

The catch-all for things that are explicitly **not** launch blockers. Done iteratively as time allows, alongside the other phases — none of these gate a release.

**Why a separate phase**: the spec is explicit that the recommendation model, store-submission polish, and offline tolerance are not launch blockers. Putting them in their own epic signals 'park here, don't let it expand the launch scope.'

**Ordering note**: depends on E9. Children 9.1, 9.2, 9.3 are independent and can ship in any order.

title: 8.2 Social: follow / like / comment / view (RLS-protected)
description:
The follow / like / comment / view interactions, all backed by the `follows` and `engagements` tables from E6. RLS is the source of truth — every interaction is server-validated.

**Files**
- `app/lib/features/social/follow_button.dart`
- `app/lib/features/social/engagement_bar.dart` — like, comment, share, view-count.
- `app/lib/features/social/comments_sheet.dart`
- `backend/supabase/functions/engagement/index.ts` — single Edge Function for all four engagement types (router pattern); enforces `auth.uid()` server-side.
- `backend/supabase/migrations/0004_engagement_views.sql` — a view that joins `videos` + `engagements` for fast feed rendering.

**Validation**
- Follow a user → their videos appear in your 'Following' feed within the next refresh.
- A like is idempotent (liking twice doesn't double-count).
- A forged `user_id` in a like/comment payload is rejected at the Edge Function layer (not the client).
- View counts increment on a clip after 2+ seconds of visible playback (not on every page impression).

**Agent**: code-puppy + code-critic (RLS review).
**Notes**: the engagement bar is the second-most visible UI element after the video. Don't make it look like 2014 Twitter.

title: 8.1 Calendar: dated events + local reminders + FCM push
description:
A simple dated list (NOT a full calendar grid in v1) of `calendar_events`: planned workouts, classes, goals. Local reminders via the platform scheduler; FCM push for server-side reminders.

**Files**
- `app/lib/features/calendar/event_list_page.dart` — dated list view.
- `app/lib/features/calendar/event_create_page.dart`
- `app/lib/features/calendar/local_reminders.dart` — wraps `flutter_local_notifications`.
- `backend/supabase/functions/calendar-reminders/index.ts` — Edge Function: a scheduled job (via `pg_cron` or Supabase scheduled functions) that fires FCM at the configured lead time.

**Validation**
- Create an event for 'tomorrow at 8am' → a local notification fires at the device's local 7:50am (10-min default lead).
- FCM reminder reaches a device that has been backgrounded for an hour.
- Deleting an event cancels its local reminder.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: the spec says 'keep it a simple dated list' — that's a deliberate scope cut. A full calendar grid is a v2 problem.

title: E9 — Phase 8: Calendar + social graph (Part B · app) [~2-3 weeks]
description:
**Phase 8 (Part B · app) — ~2-3 weeks · priority normal**

Two distinct features in one phase: a simple dated calendar of workouts/classes/goals, and the follow/like/comment/view social graph. Both already have data model support from E6; this phase is UI + state + RLS-backed interactions.

**Why they're grouped**: they share the social identity model (who you follow, what you can see) and the FCM push wiring. Doing them together avoids two passes through the same cross-cutting concerns.

**Ordering note**: depends on E8 (you'll want to test calendar/social interactions with real activity data). Children 8.1 and 8.2 are parallel.

title: 7.2 Link a clip to an activity (the distinguishing feature)
description:
The feature that distinguishes this app from a generic short-video app: when you upload a clip of a run, the clip carries the run's stats (distance, pace, splits, elevation).

**Files**
- `backend/supabase/migrations/0003_video_activity_link.sql` — `videos.activity_id` is already a column; this adds the index + a join view.
- `app/lib/features/upload/attach_activity_step.dart` — upload wizard step: 'link to which workout?'.
- `app/lib/features/feed/feed_item_overlay.dart` — overlay shows the linked activity's stats below the caption.
- `app/lib/features/activity/activity_detail_page.dart` — tap a workout → see all clips linked to it.

**Validation**
- Upload a clip with an activity attached → feed shows the activity stats in the overlay.
- A clip uploaded without an activity shows a 'no stats' placeholder (not an error).
- Tapping the overlay opens the activity detail page; activity detail page lists the clip.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is the bit that makes the app *not* another TikTok clone. Spend time on the overlay design — it should be glanceable, not a wall of numbers.

title: 7.1 HealthKit (iOS) + Health Connect (Android) + GPS
description:
Platform entitlements, permissions UX, and the recording loop. `health` package for HealthKit/Health Connect; `geolocator` for GPS. On-device only; sync is a separate concern (E10).

**Files**
- `app/lib/features/activity/recorder.dart` — the recording loop.
- `app/lib/features/activity/summary.dart` — the summary record shape.
- `ios/Runner/Info.plist` — `NSHealthShareUsageDescription`, `NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription`, `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`, `NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription`.
- `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` — Health Connect permissions, foreground service for ongoing workouts.
- `app/pubspec.yaml` — `health`, `geolocator`, `permission_handler`.

**Validation**
- iOS: a real device run of a 20-min walk → HealthKit shows the activity → app shows the same summary.
- Android: same, against Health Connect.
- Permission denial flow is graceful — clear message, no crash, can re-request from settings.
- App-killed-mid-workout case: foreground service keeps recording on Android; iOS uses HealthKit's own workout session, which is robust to kills.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: the platform permissions UX is half the work. The first build of this task will be a lot of plist/manifest churn. Budget for it.

title: E8 — Phase 7: Activity tracking (Part B · app) [~1.5-3 weeks]
description:
**Phase 7 (Part B · app) — ~1.5-3 weeks · priority normal**

HealthKit on iOS, Health Connect on Android, via the Flutter `health` package. GPS via `geolocator`. Record on-device; sync **summary** records only — raw GPS points stay on the device in v1.

**Why summaries only**: uploading raw GPS is a privacy / cost / battery triple-threat. Summaries (distance, duration, splits, elevation gain, average pace) are what the social feed actually displays anyway.

**Ordering note**: depends on E7 (you'll want to test activity-to-video linking against a real feed). Children 7.1 and 7.2 are tightly coupled (7.2 is the point of 7.1).

title: 6.3 Simple ranking (chronological 'following' + 'discover' by recency × engagement)
description:
Two feed sources. NO recommendation model — that's explicitly NOT a launch blocker (it's parked in E10).

**Files**
- `backend/supabase/functions/feed-following/index.ts` — Edge Function: returns the latest `ready` videos from accounts the user follows, paginated.
- `backend/supabase/functions/feed-discover/index.ts` — Edge Function: returns the latest `ready` videos from accounts the user doesn't follow, sorted by `recency * engagement_score`.
- `app/lib/features/feed/feed_source.dart` — toggles between the two sources.

**Validation**
- 'Following' is empty for a new user with no follows → shows a friendly empty state.
- 'Discover' is non-empty on a fresh DB (you'll need to seed it manually for testing).
- A new video uploaded to a followed account appears in 'Following' within ~5 seconds (no aggressive polling; consider a Realtime channel).

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: keep the engagement score dead simple — `(likes*1 + comments*2 + views*0.1) / hours_since_post`. No ML. The point is to launch.

title: 5.3 Auth via Supabase Auth (no custom auth!)
description:
Wire email + Apple + Google sign-in through Supabase Auth. Do not roll your own auth.

**Files**
- `app/lib/features/auth/` — sign-in screens, OAuth callbacks.
- `backend/supabase/config.toml` — auth providers enabled.

**Validation**
- Email/password sign-up creates a `users` row via a Postgres trigger on `auth.users`.
- Sign in with Apple and Sign in with Google work on iOS and Android respectively (manual device test).
- Sign-out clears the Supabase session and the local cache; restart of the app lands on the sign-in screen.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is a 600-line task, not a 60-line task. The 'thin slice' is about scope (just auth), not about effort. Apple Sign-In in particular has annoying config in both Xcode and Supabase.

title: 5.2 Supabase migrations: full data model + RLS
description:
Migrations for the full relational model and the RLS policies that gate every read/write. **This is the security surface — review it twice.**

**Files**
- `backend/supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql` — schema for: `users` (extends `auth.users`), `activities`, `videos` (with `activity_id` FK), `calendar_events`, `follows`, `engagements` (likes/comments/views).
- `backend/supabase/migrations/0002_rls.sql` — RLS policies for every table.
- `backend/rls/README.md` — one-paragraph rationale per policy.

**Critical RLS rules**
- A user can read another user's **public** video metadata but NOT their activity GPS points (those are private, server-side summary only — see E8).
- A user can only INSERT an engagement with their own `user_id`; the `auth.uid()` check is non-negotiable.
- Follows are mutual-readable; only the follower can create/delete their own follow.
- Calendar events are owner-only; no public calendar feed in v1.

**Validation**
- `supabase db reset` runs migrations cleanly.
- A test script hits each table as anon, as authenticated user A on A's rows, and as authenticated user B on A's rows — only the expected combinations succeed.
- A write with a forged `user_id` is rejected at the DB layer, not at the client.

**Agent**: code-puppy + code-critic (security review of the RLS file before merge).
**Notes**: Postgres, not Firestore, was chosen for exactly this — RLS is a first-class feature. Use it.

title: 5.1 Flutter scaffold + Supabase client + env config + Sentry
description:
Scaffold the Flutter app, feature-first folder layout, wire the Supabase client, env config, and Sentry from day one.

**Files**
- `app/lib/core/` — `supabase_client.dart`, `env.dart`, `sentry.dart`, `router.dart`.
- `app/lib/features/auth/` — auth feature module (UI + state, real implementation in 5.3).
- `app/pubspec.yaml` — `supabase_flutter`, `flutter_dotenv`, `sentry_flutter`, etc.
- `app/.env` (gitignored) + `app/.env.example` (committed).

**Validation**
- `flutter run` boots a hello-world that initializes Supabase and Sentry on startup (visible in logs).
- A throwaway unhandled exception in dev shows up in Sentry's dashboard within a minute.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: feature-first (`features/<name>/{ui,state,data}/`) not layer-first (`screens/`, `widgets/`, `services/`). It's the boring choice for a small app but the only one that scales when the video feed lands.

title: E6 — Phase 5: App foundation — Auth + thin slice (Part B · app) [~1-2 weeks]
description:
**Phase 5 (Part B · app) — ~1-2 weeks · priority normal**

The first app code. Scaffold the Flutter project, wire the Supabase client, get a real auth flow working end-to-end, and stand up the full data model with RLS. Nothing user-facing is impressive yet — the goal is to prove the foundation is solid before the make-or-break video phase.

**Why this is its own phase**: the data model + RLS policies are the **entire authz surface**. Get them wrong here and you've shipped a security hole that you can't easily unwind after launch.

**Ordering note**: depends on E5 (the agent-generated backlog). Children 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 can run mostly in parallel; 5.2 must land before 5.3 if you want auth to talk to a real schema.

title: 4.3 Self-review: delegate planning-agent/ to code-critic
description:
Before declaring Part A done, hand the `planning-agent/` tree to `code-critic` for a self-review. This is the meta-loop: the agent that produces backlogs gets one too.

**Files**
- `docs/reviews/planning-agent-review.md` — the review output.
- Any issues raised → new tasks filed under this epic and resolved before closing E4.

**Validation**
- `code-critic` runs against `planning-agent/src/**/*.py` + prompts.
- Output covers: prompt injection surface, error paths, the human gate's default-deny behavior, idempotency of the writer, and the termination guards' correctness.
- No P0/P1 findings open at the end of E4.

**Agent**: code-critic
**Notes**: this is the moment to surface design problems, not after you've started building the app. A weak critic here is a weak foundation for the bridge milestone.

title: 4.2 Idempotent writer: local files (docs/backlog/)
description:
After the human gate approves, write the tree to LOCAL files. Stable IDs and content hashes so re-runs don't duplicate or churn.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/src/writers/local_md.py` — emits `docs/backlog/index.md`, `docs/backlog/<epic-id>.md`, per-task sections.
- `planning-agent/src/writers/local_json.py` — emits `docs/backlog/backlog.json` with the full tree + critic report.
- `planning-agent/src/writers/github_issues.py` — OPTIONAL, behind a feature flag. Uses GitHub Issues REST, not the (unavailable) MCP.

**Why local files, not Jira/Linear**: the original spec assumed MCP for Jira/Linear. This env has no MCP. For a solo dev, a clean `docs/backlog/` is genuinely enough for v1.

**Idempotency**
- Each node's content includes a stable hash of (id, title, description, estimate_days, depends_on). If a re-run produces the same hash for a node, do NOT rewrite that file.
- If a node was removed since last run, leave a tombstone (or delete; document the choice).

**Validation**
- First run: produces `docs/backlog/index.md` and one file per epic + a `backlog.json`.
- Second run with NO spec change: zero diff in `docs/backlog/` (`git status` clean).
- Re-run with a spec edit: only the changed node's file differs; all other files are byte-identical.
- `github_issues.py` is reachable but is OFF by default; turning it on requires an explicit `--sync-github` flag and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` env var.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is also a security boundary. The writer must NEVER touch files outside `docs/backlog/` (no path-traversal, no symlink escapes).

title: 4.1 Human-approval gate (BEFORE any write)
description:
A non-optional gate that blocks any write to disk or any external tracker until a human has approved the assembled tree.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/src/review_gate.py` — `request_approval(tree, critic_report) -> ApprovalResult`.

**Behavior**
- Renders a human-readable preview of the tree (Markdown) and the critic report.
- Explicit prompt: 'Approve / Reject / Edit-then-Approve'. In CI / non-interactive mode, default to REJECT (never silently approve).
- Audit log: timestamp, decision, what was changed if 'Edit'.

**Validation**
- Non-interactive run (no TTY, no `--yes`) → writes are blocked; clear log entry explains why.
- Interactive run with `--yes` for the case 'we already reviewed this offline' → proceeds and logs that the human gate was bypassed by explicit flag.
- A pure-CI run (e.g. in a PR) cannot accidentally write to `docs/backlog/`.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is a security boundary, not a UX nicety. Treat it like one. Default-deny is the only safe default.

title: E4 — Phase 4: Backlog writer + human gate (Part A · agent) [~3-5 days]
description:
**Phase 4 (Part A · agent) — ~3-5 days · priority normal**

The last agent-only phase. Adds the **non-optional human gate** and an **idempotent writer** to local files. The env has no MCP/web-search, so the v1 target is local Markdown + JSON in `docs/backlog/`; GitHub Issues sync is optional.

**Why the human gate is non-optional for v1**: the spec is explicit. A planning agent that writes to a tracker without a human in the loop is a footgun. v1 keeps humans in the loop; v2 can revisit.

**Ordering note**: depends on E3 (critic + graph). Children 4.1 → 4.2 → 4.3 in sequence (gate must exist before writer; review follows writes).

title: 3.2 Build depends_on edges + compute build order
description:
Wire the `depends_on` edges from the tree (some are explicit in node fields; others are inferred from parent-child relationships and from the critic's findings) and compute a build order + critical path.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/src/task_graph.py` (extend, or merge with the E2 module)
- `planning-agent/src/build_order.py` — topological sort + critical-path computation.

**Validation**
- Given a tree, produces a deterministic build order (e.g. lexicographic, or by depth-first on the `id` tree — pick one and document it).
- Critical-path output: list of node ids on the longest dependency chain, with total `estimate_days`.
- A cycle in `depends_on` → raises a clear error (not a hang). `bd dep cycles` is a good cross-check.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: use Python's `graphlib.TopologicalSorter` rather than hand-rolling topo sort. Boring is good.

title: 3.1 Critic persona (bounded, 1-2 passes)
description:
Build the Critic-LLM that audits the task tree the orchestrator produced. Bounded re-planning: at most 2 re-plan passes; after that, write the open concerns into a `critic_open_questions.md` and stop.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/prompts/critic.md` — the critic persona + rubric.
- `planning-agent/src/critic.py` — `audit(tree: list[Node]) -> CriticReport`.

**Critic rubric (must check)**
- **Gaps**: anything in the spec that no node addresses (look for verbs like 'secure', 'authenticate', 'log', 'monitor' that imply cross-cutting work).
- **Ordering**: dependencies that are wrong (B depends on A but is listed before A).
- **Cross-cutting**: explicit checks for auth, CI, observability, error handling, rate-limiting — if any are missing from the tree, flag them.
- **Granularity**: any leaf over 1 day that should have been decomposed.

**Validation**
- Feed it the E2 output for the architecture spec → produces a critic report with concrete, actionable findings (not vague 'looks good').
- Run critic → orchestrator → critic a second time → either clean or new findings are minor; never a third re-plan.
- Adversarial input (a deliberately incomplete spec) → critic catches the gap in one pass.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: the critic's output should be *structured* too (a Pydantic `CriticReport`), not free-text. The writer (E4) will render it as a section in the human-gate review.

title: E3 — Phase 3: Critic pass + dependency mapping (Part A · agent) [~4-6 days]
description:
**Phase 3 (Part A · agent) — ~4-6 days · priority normal**

Add a bounded Critic-LLM that reviews the assembled task tree for gaps, wrong ordering, and missing cross-cutting work (auth, CI, observability). Plus the dependency-edge + build-order logic.

**Why the critic is bounded**: an unbounded critic will keep finding 'one more thing' and the agent will spiral. Hard cap of 1-2 re-plan passes; after that, escalate to a human.

**Ordering note**: depends on E2 (needs a finished tree to critique). Children 3.1 and 3.2 can run in parallel.

title: 2.1 Deterministic orchestrator + stop guards
description:
Implement the orchestrator loop and the three termination guards. The loop is plain Python — only the planner call itself is an LLM.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/src/orchestrator.py` — `run(spec: str) -> list[Node]` (in-memory; writer comes in E4).
- `planning-agent/src/task_graph.py` — Node collection, `id` generation, parent/child wiring.

**Stop guards (all three must trip before recursion halts)**
1. **Max depth 4** — refuse to recurse past depth 4 regardless of `needs_decomposition`.
2. **Granularity test** — if a node is at the leaf-eligible depth AND `estimate_days <= 1.0` AND has a clear done-condition in `description`, stop.
3. **Total node budget** — hard cap on total nodes (e.g. 200) to prevent runaway on adversarial specs.

**Logging requirement**
- Every planner call logged: depth, node id being decomposed, resulting children ids, which guard (if any) stopped the recursion.
- Log format: structured (JSON lines), not free-text, so the writer (E4) can render a clean audit trail.

**Validation**
- Run on the architecture spec → produces a multi-level tree where leaves are atomic (≤1 day) and the tree respects all three guards.
- Manually flip a leaf's `needs_decomposition` to True and re-run → guard (1) or (2) kicks in, no infinite loop.
- Hit guard (3) on a synthetic spec that asks for unlimited decomposition → stops with a clear log message.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is the *core* of the agent. Time-box it. If the loop logic isn't clean by day 2, that's the signal to redesign before going further.

title: E2 — Phase 2: Recursion loop + termination conditions (Part A · agent) [~4-6 days]
description:
**Phase 2 (Part A · agent) — ~4-6 days · priority normal**

Add a **deterministic** orchestrator (plain code, not LLM) that loops over nodes from E1, recurses into any node with `needs_decomposition=True`, and stops on **all three** termination guards.

**Why the orchestrator is plain code, not an LLM**: the loop, the guards, and the logging are not decisions — they're a state machine. Putting them in the LLM is exactly the kind of 'we'll figure it out at runtime' that creates the runaway recursion the spec explicitly warns against.

**Ordering note**: depends on E1 (needs the planner and the schema). Single-task epic; subtask is one larger piece of work.

title: 1.2 Planner persona + prompt (one-level, no recursion)
description:
Build the Planner-LLM wrapper: a prompt + a thin Python function that calls the LLM, parses JSON output into `Node`s, validates, and prints.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/prompts/planner.md` — the planner persona + instructions.
- `planning-agent/src/planner.py` — `decompose_one_level(spec: str) -> list[Node]`.

**Prompt contract (must enforce)**
- Output **structured JSON only** — an array of `Node` objects, depth 0/1.
- Hard instruction: do NOT recurse, do NOT write to disk, do NOT call any tool.
- Refuse to break the schema; emit a refusal message rather than a malformed node.

**Validation**
- Feed it the architecture spec → produces a list of clean top-level epics (one per phase 0-9 plus the bridge).
- Each epic is a valid `Node` (no `ValidationError`).
- No nested children beyond depth 1 (one-level deep only).
- An obviously-garbage spec produces a clean refusal, not a stack trace.

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this phase deliberately has NO orchestrator and NO writer. Output goes to stdout. The next phase (E2) wires the loop.

title: 1.1 Define node schema (Pydantic)
description:
Define the `Node` Pydantic model — the contract every phase of the planning agent will share.

**Files**
- `planning-agent/src/schema.py`

**Schema fields (per spec)**
- `id: str` — stable, slugified, e.g. `E1-1.1`.
- `title: str`
- `description: str`
- `parent_id: Optional[str]` — null for epics at depth 0.
- `estimate_days: float` — must be > 0 when `needs_decomposition=False` (i.e. at leaves).
- `depends_on: list[str]` — other `id`s.
- `needs_decomposition: bool` — true when the planner wants the orchestrator to recurse.

**Validation**
- `from schema import Node; Node(id='E1-1.1', title='x', description='y', parent_id=None, estimate_days=1.0, depends_on=[], needs_decomposition=False)` succeeds.
- `Node(... estimate_days=-1 ...)` raises `ValidationError`.
- `Node(... depends_on=['nope'] ...)` is permitted (string IDs are not FK-validated at the Pydantic layer — that's the orchestrator's job).

**Agent**: code-puppy
**Notes**: this is the only schema in v1. Keep it strict — no optional extras, no 'we might need this later' fields. The Zen of Python applies: 'There should be one — and preferably only one — obvious way to do it.'

title: E1 — Phase 1: One-shot planner with strict schema (Part A · agent) [~3-5 days]
description:
**Phase 1 (Part A · agent) — ~3-5 days · priority normal**

The simplest version of the planning agent: a Planner-LLM that decomposes a spec **one level deep** into epics. No recursion, no orchestrator, no writer — just `prompt + LLM + parse + print`. Goal is to lock the **schema** (the contract every later phase will share) and prove the planner can produce clean top-level structure from the architecture spec.

**Why this is its own phase**: the schema is the most expensive thing to change later. Every subsequent phase reads/writes the same `Node` shape. Get it right here.

**Ordering note**: depends on E0 (need the `planning-agent/` directory). Children 1.1 and 1.2 are tightly coupled (1.2 cannot run without 1.1's schema).
